def: A non-zero vector that a square matrix only stretches, so that Av = lambda v.
The factor lambda by which a matrix stretches one of its eigenvectors.
Repeatedly multiplying a vector by a matrix and renormalising, which converges to the top eigenvector.
A matrix equal to its transpose; it has real eigenvalues and perpendicular eigenvectors.
A square matrix whose columns are perpendicular unit vectors, so that Q^T Q = I; it rotates or reflects without stretching.
The symmetric matrix of covariances between features, X^T X/(n-1) for centred data.
Finding the orthogonal directions of greatest variance in data as the eigenvectors of its covariance matrix.
The factorisation A = U Sigma V^T of any matrix into a rotation, an axis-aligned stretch and another rotation.
The non-negative diagonal entries of Sigma in the SVD, which measure how much the matrix stretches along each pair of singular vectors.
The number of linearly independent columns of a matrix, equal to its number of non-zero singular values.
The sum of the first k terms of the SVD, which is the best rank-k approximation of a matrix.
The result that the truncated SVD is the closest rank-k matrix to A, with error set by the discarded singular values.
The square root of the sum of all squared entries of a matrix.
Replacing a matrix by a product of thin factors so that it needs far fewer numbers.
